 Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The applicant is in judicial custody in Fir No.36 of 2024, dated 25.02.2024, under Sections 363,
376 Ipc and Sections 3/4 of The Protection Of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
The instant FIR has been lodged at the instance of police, who questioned the victim.
The victim revealed that she is 17 years of age.
She is in the relationship with the applicant for 1 years prior to lodging of the FIR.
On 14.12.2023, they both left their houses and married in a temple at Pithoragarh.
When the victim was questioned, she was pregnant.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant and the victim, both are in relationship; the applicant is 21 years of age; the victim is still pregnant; the FIR per se reveals that both are married.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that as per instructions, the marriage was not solemnized as per law.

6. In the cases of Mahesh Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine Del 2634, Faizan Wahid Baig v. The State of Maharashtra, MANU/MHOR/62774/2022, Vijaylakshmi and another v. State and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Mad 317, Shri John Franklin Shylla v. State of Meghalaya & Anr.,
2023 SCC OnLine Megh 303 and Ashik Ramjali Ansari v. State of Maharashtra and another, 2023 SCC OnLine Bom 1390, the Courts have either granted bail or quashed the proceedings or acquitted the accused in the cases like instant one.

sentences.text:
9. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant or any of his relatives shall not make any contact with the victim, in any manner, whatsoever, either physically, electronically or by any other means.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to Court or any Police Officer and the applicant should not tamper with evidence.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 16.05.2024 Sanjay Dinesh Giri vs State Of Uttarakhand on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22130442/
